header.name: Point Set Topology
header.description: The subject of topology serves to lay the foundations for future study in Analysis, in Geometry, and in Algebraic Topology. In general terms, Topology concerns itself with properties of geometric objects and mappings between them such as continuity, connectedness, compactness, deformation. In this course we study Point Set Topology which is the branch of Topology dealing with the basic set-theoretic definitions and constructions used in Topology. The core of the study will cover topological spaces, connectedness, compactness (through compactness of finite products), and the countability and separation axioms (through the Urysohn metrization theorem), and complete metric spaces. The course will prepare the student to undertake further studies in the areas mentioned above.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to determine whether a given set is open or closed.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to determine whether a given mapping between topological spaces is continuous. They will also be able to construct continuous mappings.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to determine whether a given set is connected; and whether a given set is compact.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to determine whether a given topological space is first countable; or second countable; or normal; or metrizable, or a metric space is complete.
